attachments.insertion_landmark: superior sclera, ~7mm posterior to the corneal limbus

functional_compartments.name: Single fiber population
functional_compartments.function_note: True insertion is onto the sclera of the eyeball, not a fixed bony point; the eyeball is not modeled as its own rigid body with rotational DOF in this pass (a natural candidate for a small future extension), so this muscle's insertion is given relative to the orbital bone frame as an engineering approximation of its resting position rather than a moving attachment.
functional_compartments.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

motor_endplate_zones.reference_line_to: muscle origin at the common tendinous ring (annulus of Zinn)
motor_endplate_zones.notes: Range across 20 specimens for the distance from the scleral insertion to the anterior-most termination of the intramuscular oculomotor nerve arborization, expressed as % of total muscle length; the terminal nerve plexus (site of highest motor endplate density) clusters near this point, close to mid-muscle length. Compared directly against inferior rectus in the same study; both share the same general Y-shaped arborization pattern.
motor_endplate_zones.source: Haladaj R, Polguj M, Tubbs RS, 'Comparison of the Superior and Inferior Rectus Muscles in Humans: An Anatomical Study with Notes on Morphology, Anatomical Variations, and Intramuscular Innervation Patterns', Biomed Res Int 2020:9037693, doi:10.1155/2020/9037693 (https://doi.org/10.1155/2020/9037693) -- 20 SR specimens, Sihler staining, PMC7210515 -- retrieved via PubMed

source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

ultrasound_injection_approach.transducer_placement: EMG-needle approach, not ultrasound: with the globe anesthetized topically and gently rotated into infraduction to put SR on stretch, a fine monopolar EMG needle is passed percutaneously (or trans-conjunctivally through the superior fornix) toward the muscle belly a few millimeters posterior to its scleral insertion (~7mm behind the limbus), then advanced while the awake patient is asked to look up (elevate) so contraction-related EMG activity at the needle tip confirms intramuscular placement before injecting.
ultrasound_injection_approach.depth_layer: Superficial extraocular/sub-Tenon plane just posterior to the insertion; the belly is thin (~9N max isometric force), so only a few millimeters of needle travel separate conjunctiva from the globe wall.
ultrasound_injection_approach.identification_cues: EMG discharge that increases with attempted elevation (and with intorsion/adduction, its secondary actions) confirms the needle tip is in SR rather than in Tenon's fascia or an adjacent muscle.
structures_at_risk: globe (perforation risk, given the short, thin muscle belly and the needle tip's proximity to the sclera)

levator palpebrae superioris, which lies immediately superficial to SR for most of its course and shares a fascial sheath with it -- diffusion here is the usual cause of inadvertent ptosis after SR injection
superior oblique tendon, which crosses under SR near the superonasal globe
ultrasound_injection_approach.notes: SR is only occasionally injected directly (most often for a vertical deviation such as dissociated vertical deviation, or paired with an antagonist injection); the EMG-guided percutaneous technique described here follows the method Alan Scott's group documents for extraocular muscle injection generally, most thoroughly published for the horizontal recti. Guidance is by needle-tip EMG, never ultrasound, in real clinical practice.
ultrasound_injection_approach.source: Debert I, Miller JM, Danh KK, Scott AB, 'Pharmacologic injection treatment of comitant strabismus', J AAPOS 20(2):106-111.e2 (2016), doi:10.1016/j.jaapos.2015.11.011 (https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jaapos.2015.11.011) -- EMG-guided technique description, PMC4833878; Hariharan P, Balzer JR, Anetakis K, Crammond DJ, Thirumala PD, 'Electrophysiology of Extraocular Cranial Nerves: Oculomotor, Trochlear, and Abducens Nerve', J Clin Neurophysiol 35(1):11-15 (2018), doi:10.1097/WNP.0000000000000417 (https://doi.org/10.1097/WNP.0000000000000417) -- review noting EMG-guided botulinum injection in strabismus -- both retrieved via PubMed
